PullRequest.Title: Add multi-file diff editor with optional file list widget
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request introduces a new composite widget, `MultiDiffEditorWithFileListWidget`, which integrates the existing multi-file diff editor with an optional file list displayed on the right. Key changes include:

- **New Composite Widget**: The `MultiDiffEditorWithFileListWidget` wraps the existing `MultiDiffEditorWidget` and a new `MultiDiffEditorFileList`, allowing users to view file changes alongside diffs.
- **File List Functionality**: The file list shows the status of each file (Added/Modified/Deleted/Renamed) and allows navigation to the corresponding diff by clicking or pressing Enter.
- **User Options**: Introduced an experimental setting, `multiDiffEditor.experimental.fileList`, to toggle the file list's visibility. The default is off, preserving the original editor for users who do not opt in.
- **Menu Updates**: Added a "Files View & Position" submenu in the editor's menu for toggling between list/tree views and positioning the file list on the left or right.
- **Styling Adjustments**: Ensured the file list hover matches the Explorer's style, applying consistent padding and margins.

This implementation aims to enhance the user experience while maintaining the existing functionality for users who prefer the original layout. All changes have been validated with passing tests and adherence to coding standards.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The creation condition ignores hasRoom, and the added test explicitly expects fileListVisible=false while hasList=true at 500px. The file-list constructor and autorun explicitly create a tree model for every current item and subscribe to viewport changes; only prevalence and collection size vary.
Findings.PerformanceResource: The file-list widget, Workbench tree model nodes, per-item/tree-element objects, listeners, and hidden DOM infrastructure.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained objects and initial tree work grow O(number of changed files plus folder path nodes) and persist for the editor lifetime; hidden viewport synchronization additionally scales with scrolling frequency.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased open latency and retained-memory/GC pressure in narrow editor groups, with unnecessary ongoing CPU while the hidden list remains subscribed.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no file-list tree or its listeners. Even within the new composite, a disabled list is cleared; only the new responsive-hidden path retains the full widget despite rendering none of it.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Enabling the experiment now constructs and retains the complete file-list widget even when the editor is narrower than 400 + 160 pixels and the split view immediately hides that widget.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 127-137 compute hasRoom but instantiate MultiDiffEditorFileList whenever enabled, before applying visible = enabled && hasRoom; line 133 is the eager construction point.
Findings.Title: Defer the file-list tree until it can be shown
Findings.Impact: Opening an enabled multi-diff editor in a narrow/split editor group performs O(N) tree construction and retains the list/tree nodes for the editor lifetime even though no file list can be displayed; subsequent diff scrolling also continues list synchronization work. Large commits or SCM groups therefore pay extra open-time CPU, memory, and GC cost for invisible UI.
Findings.Evidence: The autorun clears the list only when the user disables it. If enabled but too narrow, it still creates MultiDiffEditorFileList, whose constructor creates a WorkbenchCompressibleObjectTree and calls getFileListElements(...)/setChildren(...) for the full view-model item collection. It also keeps currentItem subscribed to visibleDiffItems. The PR's own responsive test records `{ fileListVisible: false, hasList: true }` at 500px, proving this hidden lifetime. SCM group and commit sources pass their full, uncapped changed-file collections.
Findings.Recommendation: Gate initial creation on `enabled && hasRoom`, and suspend or dispose the list's item/viewport observers while responsive-hidden. If tree expansion/focus must survive resize, save that small view state and restore it when recreating the visible tree.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The scroll view derives layout directly from onScroll and replaces the layout object on each update; the new file-list currentItem observable keeps visibleDiffItems observed. The changed filter/map and its O(N) cardinality are explicit. Only the exact millisecond impact varies with commit size and hardware.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread CPU plus the arrays allocated by filter and map.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows as O(number of diff items × scroll updates); equality comparison only suppresses notifications after both full scans and allocations have already occurred.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased scroll latency, CPU/GC pressure, and dropped frames on large multi-file diffs.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, scrolling ran the existing compressed-layout and render passes, but there was no visibleDiffItems observer and no extra filter/map traversal solely to synchronize a file list.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: When the file list is enabled, every scroll-layout update now performs two additional synchronous passes over all diff items and allocates intermediate/result arrays before equality suppression can prevent downstream updates.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 208-213 add a derived observable that reads the per-scroll layout and then runs filter(...).map(...) across every view item; MultiDiffEditorFileList now observes that value to follow the viewport.
Findings.Title: Avoid rescanning every diff item on each scroll
Findings.Impact: With the file list enabled, scrolling a large SCM group or commit adds O(N) synchronous CPU and short-lived array allocation to every wheel/trackpad update, increasing main-thread and GC pressure and risking dropped frames for large change sets.
Findings.Evidence: CompressedVirtualizedScrollView observes onScroll, recomputes and sets layout on each scroll update, and its existing render already loops over all items. This new derived value reads that layout and independently filters and maps the entire _viewItems array. MultiDiffEditorFileList.currentItem reads visibleDiffItems, so the derived is live whenever the optional list exists. SCM groups and history commits feed the editor's complete resource/change arrays with no cap, making hundreds or thousands of items realistic.
Findings.Recommendation: Publish visible view models from the scroll view's existing layout/render traversal (or expose a maintained visible index range) so each scroll does O(visible items) incremental work rather than another full-collection filter/map.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an enabled multi-diff editor in a wide editor group
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening waits for the existing multi-diff source, model references, and initial diff wait before setInput installs the view model. With the experiment enabled, file-list construction and setChildren then execute synchronously on the editor/UI path before the populated list is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve SCM history changes and original/modified text-model references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source-resolution request for a history item, then up to two model references per changed file; effective calls are lower for missing sides and warm/cached models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one history request and per-side model-reference resolution occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing operations must resolve before the populated view model is installed; they dominate cold content loading but are unchanged by this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read persisted file-list preferences and width.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A constant number of synchronous profile-storage reads for file-list visibility, view mode, position, and preferred width.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These file-list keys were not read before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reads occur during editor/composite creation; normally backed by the storage service's loaded state and do not scale with file count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The complete changed-file collection from an SCM group or history item; it is not capped or paginated here and can reach hundreds or thousands of files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The source resolver performs one logical SCM history request. Existing model creation can resolve original and modified sides concurrently and can fan out across items; this PR does not change that concurrency. New list/tree construction is synchronous on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The configuration and profile-width/preferences are read through existing services; source/model caches behave as before. Cold model-reference misses can resolve content providers, while warm references reuse loaded models. The new file list has no cache or coalescing layer and materializes the complete current collection once the view model arrives.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed construction path, full item mapping/tree insertion, and UI-thread placement are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact open-time impact depends on changed-file count, path depth, provider/model cache warmth, and machine speed; the synchronous O(N) tree work is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: The visible list intentionally adds collection-scaled UI work. No separate finding was filed for initial visible construction, but this scenario establishes the realistic unbounded N that makes the reported scroll-path scan material.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll a large multi-diff while the file list is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Wheel/trackpad input synchronously updates scroll layout, renders items, and now recomputes visibleDiffItems before the frame can complete. There are no remote boundaries on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of diff items multiplied by high-frequency scroll-layout updates; visible cardinality is small, but effective scanned cardinality is the full collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized browser main-thread work; scroll events/layout updates are not coalesced by the new observable beyond the scrollable's existing scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The list and tree remain warm and retained after creation. No cache removes the new per-scroll filter/map; equality suppresses downstream notifications only after the scans and allocations finish.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: onScroll feeds layout, the file list keeps visibleDiffItems observed, and the changed derived executes filter plus map over all view items.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frame loss depends on N, event rate, and hardware, but the extra two full-array passes per layout update are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the PR introduces full-collection synchronous work and allocations on every scroll update, materially increasing render-path CPU and GC pressure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or resize an enabled multi-diff in a narrow/split editor group
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cold source/model resolution remains pre-existing. After the view model arrives, hidden tree population runs synchronously; later diff scrolling continues to reach hidden list synchronization despite the split view being invisible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same one source request and up to two model references per changed file as the wide scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical content loading occurred without creating a hidden file-list tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pre-existing content resolution precedes hidden tree population; the PR does not add calls or move them earlier.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Changed-file count and folder path nodes; retention lasts for the editor lifetime, with additional work scaling with subsequent scrolls and item updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All hidden-list construction and updates are serialized on the main thread. Existing per-file model loading concurrency is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The responsive-hidden list reuses and retains its tree rather than releasing it. This preserves tree/focus state but also preserves every model node and active viewport subscription while no list is visible.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: creation ignores hasRoom, and the added test explicitly proves `fileListVisible: false` while the Monaco list still exists at 500px.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prevalence is limited to users enabling the experiment and groups narrower than 560px; memory/open-time cost depends on N and path depth.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: invisible UI eagerly builds and retains an O(N) tree and keeps hot-path subscriptions active.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle the list, switch list/tree mode, or move its position
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command performs one storage write/remove, emits the shared change, and synchronously rebuilds each active file-list tree for a view-mode change. Position changes move/relayout existing split views. This is an explicit, infrequent user action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist visibility, list/tree mode, or left/right position.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile-storage write or remove per command invocation, independent of file count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These commands and profile keys did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write triggers the shared preference event before affected UI updates settle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active composite editors times changed files for a list/tree mode switch; position and visibility operations are effectively constant per editor aside from creation/disposal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates fan out synchronously to instantiated multi-diff panes, normally bounded by visible editor groups; no async burst or external request fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Profile storage is the authoritative shared state; repeated writes of the same non-default mode are possible, while list rebuilding is guarded by observable value changes. Each currently instantiated list rebuilds once for an actual mode change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: storage-event fan-out and full tree rebuilding on actual view-mode changes are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously instantiated multi-diff panes and changed files varies, but the trigger is low-frequency and user initiated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: one persistence operation and one intentional rebuild per actual user mode change are proportionate and not a hot recurring path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate from the file list to a diff
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Click/Enter updates tree selection, reveals the existing diff item, optionally expands it, and focuses the diff. Work stays local to existing widget/layout state.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected file per interaction; tree selection lookup may depend on the existing tree model but does not initiate per-file I/O.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous interaction with no parallel boundary operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The selected item and already-resolved view models are reused; no additional content/model fetch is initiated by the file-list open handler.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _open validates the item then calls existing expand/reveal/focus methods only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reveal/layout cost depends on document geometry but does not fan out over external boundaries due to this change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression beyond the separately reported viewport-synchronization mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and scroll a multi-diff with the experiment disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The original source/model resolution and diff initialization remain the critical path; no file-list widget/tree is created.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source request and up to two model references per changed file, as before.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged existing source/model concurrency; no new UI fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: With the setting disabled, the original MultiDiffEditorWidget is selected and the new visibleDiffItems derived remains unobserved/lazy. Existing source and text-model caches are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: createEditor takes the unchanged widget branch when configuration is false.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR-added performance work because the feature defaults off.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added observables are lazy and no file-list consumer is instantiated.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 20 changed files. Reported two high-confidence regressions: full-collection filter/map work on every enabled scroll update, and eager retention of the complete file-list tree while responsive-hidden. Checked opening, scrolling, narrow layout, preference changes, navigation, cache behavior, concurrency, and transitive source/model/storage boundaries.
